rules.why: A token of the build's own informers that a poll sends back; each build has its own and no screen shows it.
When this build filled its own minute of the answer; the two builds fill theirs moments apart.
OpenCost's window runs up to the moment a build filled its minute of the answer, and so do the costs and efficiencies over it. number-check-cost.spec.ts holds these numbers to OpenCost.
The cluster's metrics at the moment each build asked, kept for its own moments. number-check-monitoring.spec.ts holds them to the Prometheus.
The dev image is built WITH_CLAUDE_CODE and the compared release tag is the one without it, not a difference in the code.
Every lease's holder renews it every few seconds; whether a renewal falls inside a build's first live frame is timing, so one build's frame can hold a lease twice and count one more.

The namespace-limited Read user is refused metrics.k8s.io on self; the 403 now says it in the cluster's words where the old build, reading the answer without its body, said "get node metrics (status 403): unknown".

self has no metrics-server: the reads say metrics.k8s.io is not served, a 404 "the server could not find the requested resource" as top-resources words it, where the old build answered an empty list. k8s-service reads it from the cluster's API discovery, the same for every user, so the namespace-limited Read user, whom the cluster refuses those lists, reads it too where the old build gave it the 403.

self has no metrics-server: the namespace-limited Read user's top nodes say metrics.k8s.io is not served, "the server could not find the requested resource", from the cluster's API discovery as every user's do, where the old build asked and read the cluster's 403 without its body as "unknown".
